meta.note: Pure data. The engine reads this; questions are never hand-coded into a page. Five scenarios per axis across three acts of ten; every scenario carries four options plus an honest exit (rendered by the engine, overridden here via 'x').

O.name: Openness
O.sub: novelty of ideas · the unfamiliar · curiosity

N.name: Sensitivity
N.sub: how loudly the alarm system runs

R.name: Risk appetite
R.sub: tolerance of downside with real stakes

questions.s: You arrive at a party where the only person you know is the host — and they're busy in the kitchen.

opts.t: Pick up a tea towel and help — it gives you a job, and people drift to the kitchen anyway
Walk up to the nearest group and introduce yourself cold
Find one other person standing alone and talk to them
Post up somewhere quiet with your phone and plan an early exit

questions.s: Fridge, evening. The yoghurt is four days past its date. It looks fine. It smells… fine?

opts.t: Eat it without ceremony — dates are a suggestion, the nose is the law
Full tribunal — look, smell, tiny exploratory taste — then trust the verdict
Bin it. No yoghurt is worth a bad Tuesday night.
Eat it — then spend the evening quietly monitoring yourself for symptoms

questions.s: You get home and remember an admin task that's due in three days — twenty dull minutes, nothing more.

opts.t: Do it now, before coat comes off. Open loops cost more than the task does.
Calendar slot tomorrow lunchtime — scheduled is as good as done
It'll get done on day three, like always, with ten minutes to spare
It joins the pile of things you know about and don't look at

questions.s: Six of you are picking a restaurant. The majority lands on the one place you actively dislike.

opts.t: Go along and say nothing — the evening's peace is worth one bad meal
Say you're not keen and pitch an alternative, cheerfully
Suggest the group splits — two venues, meet after for drinks
Go along cheerfully — but on the record: 'noted, and the next pick is mine'

questions.s: A text from a good friend: 'Just passing your end — pop in for a cuppa? Be there in 20.' The flat is at its honest weekday level: lived-in, dishes visible, life everywhere.

opts.t: 'Door's open!' — kettle on, dishes exactly where they are. They asked for you, not a showroom.
'Yes!!' — followed by eighteen minutes of the fastest cleaning of your life
'Perfect timing — was just heading out! Café on the corner in 10?' The friend received; the flat unseen.
'This week's rammed — next week, properly?' Postpone until the flat and the self are presentable.

questions.s: A free evening, energy for exactly one thing.

opts.t: The series you already know and love — guaranteed pleasure, zero gamble
The strange documentary a friend swore would change how you see things
Start learning something with no obvious payoff, just because it pulls at you
Finally clear that nagging life-admin task — the relief IS the treat

questions.s: A brutal week finally ends. Recharging, for you, looks like—

opts.t: Cancelling everything. Cave weekend. Speak to no one.
Getting people round — other humans are where the energy comes back from
One close friend, one long walk
Out somewhere loud where nobody knows you and nothing is expected of you

questions.s: The 6:30 alarm exists because evening-you keeps designing a better morning — the run, the reading, the unhurried start. It is now 6:30. Mid-November. Dark.

opts.t: Up on the first note. The decision was made last night — 6:30-you is just the courier.
The designed snooze — one, nine minutes, built into the plan like a landing strip
Renegotiate from inside the duvet — and evening-you loses the case about half the time
The alarm has quietly migrated to 7:15 since the clocks changed. The better morning is a spring project now.

questions.s: Dinner with five friends. The bill arrives; you had far less than everyone else. Someone says the easy words: 'Split it six ways?'

opts.t: Split it. The £15 difference is cheaper than being the person who counts.
Say, lightly, 'I'll put in for what I had' — and let the table adjust
Split it tonight, but suggest itemising next time as a general policy
Split it — and privately eat less generously at the next three dinners to even the ledger

questions.s: 11pm, work tomorrow. A stray link has opened into a subject you didn't know existed an hour ago — and it is genuinely fascinating. Three tabs deep, night quietly disappearing.

opts.t: Follow it down. Feeling this awake to something is rarer than sleep.
Bookmark the trailhead, bed now — and genuinely return at the weekend, tabs restored, tea made
Bookmark it, bed — knowing the folder where curiosity gets saved is where curiosity goes to end
Close the tabs. It was a link-hole, not a calling — most 11pm fascination is the hour talking, not the subject.

questions.s: You sent a slightly risky message yesterday — a pitch, an overture, a hard truth. Twenty-four hours: silence.

opts.t: Reread what you sent, twice, hunting for the sentence that sank it
Genuinely forget about it until they reply — their silence is their business
Send a light follow-up nudge and move on
Decide it's a no before they can say it — quietly brace now, so the real answer can only match or improve

questions.s: Road trip, on schedule. A brown sign flashes past: something unexplained — 'The Singing Caves, 9 miles'. You've never heard of them.

opts.t: Turn off. The itinerary exists to be betrayed by better ideas.
Look them up at the next stop; detour on the way back if they're worth it
Note the name, feel the pull, keep driving — the schedule is the schedule
Nine unexplained miles each way? That's how afternoons die. Drive on, unbothered.

questions.s: The hall bulb has gone. The proper stepladder is buried behind everything else you own. The kitchen chair — the slightly wobbly one — is right there.

opts.t: Chair, now, on tiptoes. It's held you before; it can hold you again.
Excavate the ladder — two minutes of faff against six weeks in a cast is no contest
Chair, but managed: shoes off, hand on the wall, weight tested before it's trusted
Leave it dark for now. It's a hall, not an operating theatre — it can wait for a day with more ladder in it.

questions.s: Checking the restaurant bill at home, you find they forgot the second bottle — you're £40 up, the place is a ten-minute walk away, and no one will ever know.

opts.t: Walk back tomorrow and pay it — the ten minutes IS the point
Pay it next time you're passing — if you remember, and you might not
Keep it. Their systems, their margin for error — it evens out across a lifetime of being overcharged.
Keep it, but tip roughly that much extra there over the next few visits

questions.s: The kitchen drawer that needs a shove and a prayer has needed them for four months. Tonight it sticks completely — then gives.

opts.t: Toolbox out now. Four months of shoving ends tonight.
Add it to the list — the real one you actually work through on weekends
Another shove, another prayer. It works. This is the system now.
Watch a fix-it video, buy nothing, feel briefly like someone who fixes drawers

questions.s: Four-hour train ride. You've been saving a book for this. The person next to you is friendly, chatty — and clearly settling in for a long conversation.

opts.t: Put the book away — a real conversation with a stranger is rarer than a good book
Chat warmly for ten minutes, then say, with a smile, that you've been promising yourself this book all week
Answer politely but ever more briefly until they take the hint
Headphones in at the first pause — kindly, but immediately

questions.s: Results arrive Friday — a test, a scan, a decision on something that matters. It's Monday.

opts.t: Fill the week deliberately so full that Friday has no room to echo
It surfaces a few times a day; you notice it, breathe, and it passes
Low-grade static all week — sleep thinner, fuse shorter, everything slightly harder
Decide the likely outcome now and pre-live it, so Friday can only confirm or pleasantly surprise

questions.s: Mid-conversation, someone mentions — just in passing — a thing you've always vaguely wondered about. They clearly actually know. The conversation is about to move on.

opts.t: Stop the table: 'wait — go back. How does that actually work?'
Catch them later, one to one: 'you mentioned a thing earlier — tell me properly'
Note it on your phone to look up tonight — and actually look it up
Let it drift past. Wondering about it now and then was the comfortable bit.

questions.s: Tonight's thing genuinely matters — fixed start, no slipping in late. Door to door, it's forty minutes when everything behaves.

opts.t: Leave over an hour before. Early and bored beats late and sweating, every single time.
Fifty minutes: one honest cushion, no evening wasted standing in a foyer
Forty. Things mostly behave — and landing exactly on time is a small art.
Thirty-five, and make it up en route. The edge is half the point.

questions.s: Evening train, half-full. The person across the aisle is crying — quietly, steadily, past the point of hiding it. Every other passenger has become very interested in their phone.

opts.t: Lean over quietly: 'Sorry — is there anything I can do?' — and accept whatever comes back, including nothing
The wordless offer — a packet of tissues held out, a kind nod, no conversation attached
Leave them their privacy — public crying usually wants witnesses gone, and attention can be the heavier thing. Today might have been the exception.
Feel it hard, do nothing, and carry them home in your head all evening

questions.s: End of the month. Your account is about £180 lighter than your rough mental maths says it should be.

opts.t: Statement open, line by line, until the £180 confesses
Two-minute scan for anything obviously wrong, then let it go
Shrug — months vary, the mental maths was rough anyway
Feel a pulse of worry, resolve to check properly... and not check

questions.s: Saturday's plans are already set. Now a second invitation lands for Sunday — good people, but it's your only empty day this week.

opts.t: Go. Empty days are what invitations are for.
Decline, and say honestly that you need a day of nothing
Invent a softer excuse — 'family stuff' — and keep the day
Say maybe, then decide on the day by how you feel

questions.s: A small, odd symptom — nothing dramatic — has now hung around for a week.

opts.t: Book the GP today. Not from panic — because booked beats wondering.
Give it another week. Bodies are noisy; most noise passes.
Search it tonight — and surface forty minutes later, three conditions deep, worse off
Mention it to no one and think about it more than you'd ever admit

questions.s: A friend you respect calmly dismantles an opinion you've held for years — and their argument is annoyingly good.

opts.t: Chase it — 'go on, break the rest of it' — and enjoy the demolition
Defend it hard tonight, then quietly re-examine everything tomorrow
Concede the good points, keep the conclusion — roots deeper than arguments
Steer somewhere lighter. Dinner isn't a tribunal.

questions.s: Through the party wall, later than usual and sharper: a couple's row next door, escalating — then something breaking, then a silence that's somehow louder. You know them to nod to.

opts.t: Knock now with a pretext — 'sorry, heard a crash, everything okay?' — eyes open, tone light, mortification accepted
Listen hard for a few minutes — voices resuming would mean one thing, continued silence another — then decide
Not your wall's business — couples break things, the morning will look ordinary, and knocking makes you the odd one. The doubt can keep you up instead.
Log it properly — the date, the pattern if it becomes one — and decide now what threshold would make you act

questions.s: A close friend, glowing, announces the plan: quitting their stable job to day-trade full time. They've done four months of YouTube research. They ask what you think.

opts.t: Say plainly that you think it's a mistake, and exactly why — friendship over comfort
Ask the hard questions — runway, loss limits, plan B — and let the answers do the talking
Cheer them on. Belief is fuel, doubts are free, and they didn't ask for a risk assessment.
Voice mild, hedged concern — enough to be on record, not enough to dent the glow

questions.s: February 9th. The resolution — real, chosen, yours — has been flat on the canvas for eleven days now. Nobody else ever knew it existed.

opts.t: Restart tonight. Day one is any day you say it is — the eleven days are data, not a verdict.
Retire it out loud, on purpose: it was the wrong resolution, aimed at someone you don't actually want to be
Let it fade without a decision — by March it will simply never have happened
Rebuild it at a third of the size and start that tonight — the ambition was the bug, never the wanting

questions.s: Mid-birthday-dinner, someone taps a glass: 'You've known them longest — say a few words!' Eight faces turn to you.

opts.t: Stand up and enjoy it — you have three stories ready before you're upright
Say something short and warm, then sit down fast
Deflect with a joke and raise a toast instead — five words, glasses up, done
Point at someone else: 'They tell it better' — and mean it as escape, not generosity

questions.s: Your closest friend just got the exact thing you've been quietly chasing for two years — the house, the role, the news. Their joy is total. The celebration is Saturday, and you have until then to sort your face out.

opts.t: Go and celebrate hard, ache and all — both things are true, and their day only needs one of them
Go, perform it well enough, leave early — and be rough company for whoever's at home
Tell them the whole truth some quiet evening soon: 'overjoyed for you, and it's lit up everything I haven't got — both at once'
Ration the friendship until your own news arrives — protect it from your worst self by seeing less of them, exactly when presence counted

questions.s: Across the street, unmistakable: your close friend's partner, hand in hand with someone else. They didn't see you. By the time you're home you've rewritten it charitably four times — colleague, cousin, nothing — and believed none of them.

opts.t: Tell your friend today — just what you saw, no interpretation — and stay while it detonates, knowing you might be wrong and you're now in it either way
Go to the partner first: 'I saw. You tell them, or I will.'
Verify before igniting anything — you have one fact and four guesses, and someone's whole life is on the table
Hold it — if it's real it will surface without you; if it's innocent you'll have torched nothing. And they may one day learn you knew.
